timing.label: Slack update to the support lead (≤120 words, spoken in 90 s)
Objection 1 (technical)
timing.question: Who is accountable when the bot posts a wrong diagnosis?

timing.label: Objection 2 (commercial)
timing.question: My team will stop reading the channel if the bot posts every time.

problem.quote: Your team will stop re-posting the same complaint

approach.quote: Repeated double-charge reports are grouped into one issue

evidence.quote: In the replay that is nine reports and four problems

next_step.quote: What I need from you is a test channel and one of your agents

must_mention.point: Repeated double-charge reports are grouped into one issue linked to the first report's thread, not answered each time
must_mention.evidence_quote: Repeated double-charge reports are grouped into one issue linked to the first report's thread

must_mention.point: A shared scratchpad keeps triaged reports with channel, timestamp and reporter, the duplicates and the routing table
must_mention.evidence_quote: keep each triaged report with channel, timestamp and reporter, the duplicates under each issue, and the routing table

must_mention.point: A routing correction replied in the thread updates the routing table so later reports go to the right owner
must_mention.evidence_quote: her routing correction in the thread updated the routing table, so later reports went to fulfilment without asking again

must_mention.point: The diagnosis is written back once in the original thread with the owner tagged, and repeats only get a reaction
must_mention.evidence_quote: the diagnosis is written back once in the original thread with the owner tagged, and repeats only get a reaction

must_mention.point: Channel messages are untrusted input, so the responder runs under a network policy allowlist that blocks other hosts
must_mention.evidence_quote: channel messages are untrusted input, so a line in the runbook is not enough

must_mention.point: The same setup runs on a Microsoft Teams channel through a Teams trigger, without private channels
must_mention.evidence_quote: The same setup runs on a Microsoft Teams channel through a Teams trigger; private channels are not supported there

sentences_to_rerecord: I turned on the network policy with a three-host allowlist; the replay shows the paste host blocked, and the double charge is still linked to the open issue.

accuracy.anchor: Six of six points, each tied to a count, a setting or a thread. (anchors: 27–30 every point tied to a count, setting or file; 15–20 four of six; under 10 two or fewer)

structure.anchor: Outcome for the support team first; the update held all four headings in order; the ask has a day. (anchors: 22–25 all parts in order; 13–17 parts present but weak; under 8 problem only)

customer_relevance.anchor: Every answer said what her team will see in the channel; the replay counts were given twice. (anchors: 16–20 answered in terms of what the support team sees, with counts; 10–13 some; under 6 feature talk)

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Every segment within 5 s of target; one filler in about eight minutes. (anchors: 11–15 segments on target, under 1 filler/min; 6–8 two or more segments off; under 4 most segments off)

recovery.anchor: Both objections held acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer; objection 2 carried the replay counts. (anchors: 7–10 acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer held with numbers; 4–6 partial; under 3 no pattern)

stems: "Your team will see…" — open the update with what lands in the thread before naming the responder.
"The host it asked for was…" — name the blocked host in the checkpoint, not just "the paste host".
"Per problem that is…" — turn six posts for nine reports into one number she can repeat.
previous_run_comparison: First recorded run for dryrun on lab 08; no previous run to compare with.
